panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: Agent age: time since the host's Morpheus agent last reported. HPE: healthy within 2 minutes; over 5 minutes VME raises Host Unreachable ([HVM monitoring](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/monitoring.rst)). The value is as of the last collection, so it can read up to a minute high.

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.name AS "Host", cl.name AS "Cluster", s.power_state AS "Power", s.status AS "Status", s.ip_internal AS "IP", s.os_name AS "OS", s.platform_version AS "Version", s.max_cores AS "Cores", s.max_memory AS "Memory", (SELECT count(*) FROM servers v WHERE v.host_id = s.id AND v.present AND v.kind = 'vm') AS "VMs", (SELECT count(*) FROM servers v WHERE v.host_id = s.id AND v.present AND v.kind = 'vm' AND v.power_state = 'on') AS "Running", s.agent_version AS "Agent", s.agent_last_update AS "Agent check-in", EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - s.agent_last_update)::int AS "Agent age", s.member_status AS "Cluster member", s.maintenance AS "Maintenance", s.cpu_model AS "CPU model", s.hw_vendor || ' ' || s.hw_model AS "Hardware" FROM servers s LEFT JOIN clusters cl ON cl.id = s.cluster_id WHERE s.kind = 'host' AND s.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.id IN ($host)) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description:
Amber at 85%, red at 95% (sustained), as VME's Host/VM CPU Usage alarms. Short peaks are normal.

Colours match VME's default HVM alarm thresholds ([HVM alarms](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/alarms.rst)).

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(m.time, $__interval), s.name AS metric, avg(m.value) AS value FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'host' AND m.metric = 'cpu_pct' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.id IN ($host)) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: CPU ready (healthy < 5%, act > 10%)
panels.description:
**CPU ready** is the share of time a VM's vCPUs were ready to run but had to wait for a physical core.
VME reports it per VM as the average across its vCPUs (for a host: across the VMs on it).

| Per vCPU | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **under 5%** | Healthy | Nothing |
| **5 to 10%** | Contention: VMs are queuing for CPU | Check the host's CPU usage and vCPU:core ratio; watch the trend |
| **over 10%** | VMs are noticeably slowed | Move VMs to a quieter host, cut vCPUs on oversized VMs, or add capacity |

Look at sustained values: short spikes during backups, patching or boot storms are normal.
Too many vCPUs per physical core raises ready time for every VM on the host, so right-size large VMs first.

VME added this "CPU Ready-equivalent metric" in 9.1.0; HPE doesn't document how it's calculated or a threshold. At low load it reads several times higher than the kernel's
own measurement (*vCPU wait* on the exporter dashboards), so these thresholds err on the side of warning early.
When the two disagree, trust vCPU wait.

panels.description: VME reports one total per host for its local disks. Per-mount detail (below) needs node_exporter on the host.

panels.title: Host filesystems (node_exporter)
panels.description:
Filesystems on the HVM host itself, from node_exporter (install it with tools/install-exporters.sh).

* **Root (/)** and **/var** hold the OS, logs and libvirt state. A full root filesystem can stop VMs from starting or migrating.
* Local datastores (Directory datastores) live on these filesystems, so they fill up as VM disks grow.
* Shared datastores mounted on the host (NFS, GFS2) appear too, once per host, labelled with their VME datastore name.

Amber at 80%, red at 90%. **Days to full** projects the last 24 hours forward and is blank when usage isn't growing.
**Read-only** usually means the kernel remounted the filesystem after a disk error: investigate straight away.

panels.title: N+1 failover capacity per cluster
panels.description:
Memory allocated to running VMs, as a share of what the cluster could still hold if its largest host failed.
Each host keeps 4 GB for itself (OS, cluster services, agent, libvirt). VME treats VM memory as a reservation
(no memory overcommit by default), so **over 100% means a host failure or maintenance evacuation can't place every VM**.
HPE's rule: never allocate more than (N-1)/N of cluster memory, e.g. keep 33% free on 3 hosts
([capacity planning](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/capacity_planning.rst)).

targets.rawSql: WITH h AS (SELECT cluster_id, id, max_memory - 4294967296 AS usable FROM servers WHERE kind = 'host' AND present AND cluster_id IS NOT NULL), c AS (SELECT cluster_id, count(*) AS hosts, sum(usable) AS usable, sum(usable) - max(usable) AS n1 FROM h GROUP BY 1), v AS (SELECT h.cluster_id, sum(vm.max_memory) AS alloc FROM servers vm JOIN h ON h.id = vm.host_id WHERE vm.kind = 'vm' AND vm.present AND vm.power_state = 'on' GROUP BY 1) SELECT cl.name AS "Cluster", c.hosts AS "Hosts", c.usable AS "Usable memory", c.n1 AS "Usable if largest host fails", COALESCE(v.alloc, 0) AS "Allocated to running VMs", c.n1 - COALESCE(v.alloc, 0) AS "Headroom", 100.0 * COALESCE(v.alloc, 0) / NULLIF(c.n1, 0) AS "% of N+1 capacity" FROM c JOIN clusters cl ON cl.id = c.cluster_id LEFT JOIN v USING (cluster_id) ORDER BY 7 DESC

SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(m.time, $__interval), s.name AS metric, avg(m.value) AS value FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'host' AND m.metric = 'vm_running' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.id IN ($host)) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: vCPU : core ratio (running VMs)
panels.description: vCPUs of running VMs on the host divided by the host's cores. HPE's guidance: 1:1 for latency-sensitive workloads, 2:1 general purpose, 4:1 dev/test, 8:1 or more only for idle or bursty workloads. Over-committed CPU means more scheduling latency (CPU ready), not failures ([capacity planning](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/capacity_planning.rst)).

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.name, sum(v.max_cores)::float / NULLIF(s.max_cores, 0) AS ratio FROM servers s JOIN servers v ON v.host_id = s.id AND v.present AND v.kind = 'vm' AND v.power_state = 'on' WHERE s.kind = 'host' AND s.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.id IN ($host)) GROUP BY s.name, s.max_cores ORDER BY 2 DESC
